title: Flowcharts as testable execution models
lead: A flowchart is not decorative artwork. It shows how an algorithm chooses actions and which path a particular input follows.
why: In order processing, pricing and control systems, a wrong edge or label can become a business defect. A diagram should be testable against real inputs and code.
objectives: Distinguish actions, decisions, input/output and start/end.
Translate diagrams into C++ and concrete tests.
prerequisites: You can prepare a decision table.

concepts.definition: A conditional split with explicitly labeled outcomes.
The sequence of nodes visited by a particular input.
Tests that exercise each alternative outcome of a decision.
A property assumed to be true when control reaches a particular node.

sections.title: The transition matters more than the shape
paragraphs: Start and end define procedure boundaries. An action modifies state; input/output interacts with the outside world; a decision chooses a path. Connections need clear direction.
Without labeled true/false branches, a reader must guess which path to follow. A sound flowchart allows manual execution without consulting its author.

sections.title: Order validation before shipping price
paragraphs: Consider a delivery policy: negative order totals are invalid, orders totaling at least 1000 get free delivery, and smaller valid orders pay 150. Validation therefore precedes the threshold check.
Moving checks into the wrong order can apply a fee to invalid orders. The diagram makes the policy explicit before C++ code is written.

sections.title: Tracing inputs and covering branches
paragraphs: For -1 the result is invalid; for 999 the delivery fee is 150; for 1000 it is free. These exercise distinct execution paths.
Testing only one friendly input does not establish branch behavior. Boundary cases distinguish > from >= and catch off-by-one defects.

sections.title: Decompose complex charts
paragraphs: A high-level diagram reading 'validate order → calculate total → produce receipt' is usually clearer than a hundred small rectangles. Move inner details into subprocedures.
Specify the inputs and outputs of each component. A diagram neither replaces an interface contract nor removes the need for tests.

sections.title: Make visual models accessible and truthful
paragraphs: A diagram's labels must match the conditions in the executable code. On small screens, the same transitions need an accessible textual explanation.
An interactive diagram is still a model rather than a compiler result. Compare it against actual outputs in Code Studio.

steps: Only valid orders reach the threshold.

experiments.title: Incorrect order of checks
experiments.action: Perform the price threshold check before input validation.
experiments.prediction: An invalid order may receive an inappropriate shipping price.
experiments.verification: Move validation back to the first branch.

diagnostics.symptom: Invalid data has no path in the diagram
diagnostics.cause: The input-validation decision lacks its negative output.
diagnostics.fix: Add an explicit invalid branch ending the procedure.

practice.task: Draw a flowchart for exam-score validation.
Trace free-shipping logic at the boundary.
practice.criteria: All three input classes follow intended paths.
Validate the input, then apply a threshold and an incremental formula.

laboratory.title: Lab: a delivery fare flowchart
laboratory.challenge: Read whole kilometers. For distance<=0, print invalid. First five kilometers cost 100; every subsequent kilometer adds 20.
laboratory.starterCode: // Validate distance>0; implement the threshold and fare.
steps: Predict the output of each case.
Implement the code and compare output with the traced path.
rubric: All transitions are labeled and reachable.
C++ output matches the three tests.
Submit the diagram and source code.

assessment.question: What makes a flowchart traceable?
assessment.explanation: A reader needs both direction and branch meaning.

assessment.question: What happens with a negative order total?
assessment.explanation: Input validation precedes the threshold decision.

reflection: What happens if a false branch has no outgoing arrow?
